title: The Saga of Congress’s Jan. 6 Investigation

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、Zylran Mondani等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, a special congressional committee began investigating the January 6th attack on the United States Capitol.
sentences.zh: 周二，一个特别国会委员会开始调查1月6日针对美国国会大厦的袭击事件。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Luke Broadwater, on why it's not the kind of investigation that anybody had originally wanted.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事卢克·布罗德沃特将讲述为什么这并不是任何人最初想要的调查。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, July 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月28日，星期三。

sentences.en: Luke, you were at this hearing on Tuesday morning on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 卢克，你周二上午在国会山参加了这次听证会。

sentences.en: Can you describe the scene?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下当时的场景吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: The hearing got underway around 9.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 听证会在上午9点30分左右开始。

sentences.en: The select committee to investigate the January 6th attack on the United States Capitol will be in order.
sentences.zh: 调查1月6日美国国会大厦袭击事件的特别委员会现在开会。

sentences.en: I would say it immediately became both a somber and emotional affair.
sentences.zh: 我想说，这立刻变成了一场既沉重又感人的事件。

sentences.en: Four police officers who had defended the Capitol against a vicious attack entered the room wearing their dark blue uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 四名曾保卫国会大厦免受恶劣袭击的警官身穿深蓝色制服走进了房间。

sentences.en: And they sat down one by one.
sentences.zh: 他们一个接一个地坐下。

sentences.en: They were greeted by the lawmakers of the committee.
sentences.zh: 委员会的议员们向他们致意。

sentences.en: And one of the first things that happened in the committee room was members of the committee played a very graphic video of the violence that the officers endured that day.
sentences.zh: 委员会会议室里发生的第一件事，就是委员会成员播放了一段非常直观的视频，展示了警官们那天所遭受的暴力。

sentences.en: We can defend.
sentences.zh: 我们可以防守。

sentences.en: We got to hold what we have.
sentences.zh: 我们必须守住我们所拥有的。

sentences.en: Today, our team, 10.33, here's for the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们的团队，10点33分，这是为了国会大厦。

sentences.en: They've got the gallows set upside this Capitol building.
sentences.zh: 他们在国会大厦外架起了绞刑架。

sentences.en: It's time to start fucking using them.
sentences.zh: 是时候他妈的开始使用它们了。

sentences.en: I saw one of the officers tear up during it.
sentences.zh: 我看到其中一名警官在观看时流下了眼泪。

sentences.en: Another reached over to a fellow cop he had served with that day and put his arm around them.
sentences.zh: 另一名警官伸手搂住了那天与他并肩作战的同事。

sentences.en: And they began to tell their stories, their very personal stories about what they endured that day.
sentences.zh: 他们开始讲述自己的故事，讲述他们那天所经历的非常私人的故事。

sentences.en: A chaotic melee ensued.
sentences.zh: 随后发生了混乱的混战。

sentences.en: Terrorists pushed through the line and engaged us in hand-to-hand combat.
sentences.zh: 恐怖分子冲破防线，与我们进行了肉搏战。

sentences.en: One officer described how rioters attempted to gouge his eye out.
sentences.zh: 一名警官描述了暴徒如何试图挖出他的眼睛。

sentences.en: Several attempted to knock me over and steal my baton.
sentences.zh: 几个人试图把我撞倒并抢走我的警棍。

sentences.en: One latched onto my face and got his thumb in my right eye, attempting to gouge it out.
sentences.zh: 一个人抓住我的脸，把拇指插进我的右眼，试图把它挖出来。

sentences.en: I cried out in pain and managed to shake him off.
sentences.zh: 我痛苦地大叫，设法甩开了他。

sentences.en: And they called him a traitor as they sought to invade the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 当他们试图入侵国会大厦时，他们称他为叛徒。

sentences.en: Another woman, who was part of the mob of terrorists laying siege to the Capitol of the United States, shouted traitors.
sentences.zh: 另一名妇女，作为围攻美国国会大厦的恐怖分子暴徒的一部分，高喊着叛徒。

sentences.en: Another...
sentences.zh: 还有另一个……

sentences.en: What we were subjected that day was like something from a medieval battle.
sentences.zh: 我们那天所遭受的一切就像中世纪的战斗一样。

sentences.en: He said the day was akin to a medieval battle.
sentences.zh: 他说那天就像一场中世纪的战斗。

sentences.en: As I was swarmed by a violent mob, they began to beat me with their fists and with what felt like hard metal objects.
sentences.zh: 当我被一群暴徒围攻时，他们开始用拳头和感觉像是坚硬金属物的东西殴打我。

sentences.en: A third described being beaten unconscious and struck repeatedly with a taser.
sentences.zh: 第三名警官描述了自己被打昏，并被泰瑟枪反复电击。

sentences.en: I heard chanting from some in the crowd, get his gun and kill him with his own gun.
sentences.zh: 我听到人群中有人喊道，抢走他的枪，用他自己的枪杀了他。

sentences.en: I was electrocuted again and again and again with a taser.
sentences.zh: 我被泰瑟枪一次又一次地电击。

sentences.en: And he pleaded with his assailants telling them, I have kids.
sentences.zh: 他向袭击者恳求，告诉他们，我有孩子。

sentences.en: During the assault, I thought about using my firearm on my attackers.
sentences.zh: 在袭击过程中，我想过对袭击者使用我的枪支。

sentences.en: But I knew that if I did, I would be quickly overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 但我知道如果我这样做，我很快就会被淹没。

sentences.en: So I instead decided to appeal to any humanity they might have.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定诉诸他们可能拥有的任何人性。

sentences.en: I said as loud as I could manage, I've got kids.
sentences.zh: 我尽可能大声地说，我有孩子。

sentences.en: And a fourth officer relayed how he was called racist slurs over and over again.
sentences.zh: 第四名警官讲述了他如何一遍又一遍地被辱骂种族歧视的词汇。

sentences.en: Then the crowd, perhaps around 20 people, joined in screaming, boo, fucking nigger.
sentences.zh: 然后人群，大约20人左右，加入进来尖叫，嘘，他妈的黑鬼。

sentences.en: No one had ever, ever called me a nigger while wearing the uniform of a Capitol police officer.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人，从来没有人穿着国会警察的制服叫我黑鬼。

sentences.en: To the point where he broke down and cried in the storied rotunda of the Capitol after the horrors of that day were over.
sentences.zh: 以至于他在那天恐怖事件结束后，在国会大厦著名的圆形大厅里崩溃大哭。

sentences.en: I sat down on the bench in the rotunda with a friend of mine, who was also a black
sentences.zh: 我坐在圆形大厅的长椅上，和我的一位朋友，他也是一名黑人

sentences.en: Capitol police officer, and told him about the racial slurs I endured.
sentences.zh: 国会警察，告诉他我所忍受的种族歧视辱骂。

sentences.en: I became very emotional and began yelling.
sentences.zh: 我变得非常激动，开始大喊。

sentences.en: How the blank, could something like this happen?
sentences.zh: 这种事怎么可能发生？

sentences.en: Is this America?
sentences.zh: 这是美国吗？

sentences.en: I began sobbing.
sentences.zh: 我开始啜泣。

sentences.en: Officers came over to console me.
sentences.zh: 警官们走过来安慰我。

sentences.en: So these were four officers who had really compelling personal stories of confronting the mob.
sentences.zh: 所以这四名警官都有非常引人注目的个人故事，讲述了他们如何对抗暴徒。

sentences.en: And as the hearing went on, she recognizes gentlemen from Illinois, the lawmakers themselves on the committee also were reacting emotionally.
sentences.zh: 随着听证会的进行，她认出了来自伊利诺伊州的绅士，委员会本身的议员们也做出了情绪化的反应。

sentences.en: I never expected a day to be quite as emotional for me as it has been.
sentences.zh: 我从未想到这一天对我来说会如此感人。

sentences.en: I saw Adam Kinzinger, a Republican on the committee, break down in tears as he thanked the officers for their heroism.
sentences.zh: 我看到委员会的共和党人亚当·金辛格在感谢警官们的英勇表现时流下了眼泪。

sentences.en: You guys may, like, individually feel a little broken.
sentences.zh: 你们可能在个人层面上感到有点破碎。

sentences.en: You know, you talk about the impact of that day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你们谈论那天造成的影响。

sentences.en: But you guys won.
sentences.zh: 但你们赢了。

sentences.en: And we thank you for holding that line.
sentences.zh: 我们感谢你们守住了那条防线。

sentences.en: And I saw Stephanie Murphy, a Democrat from Florida, also become emotional as she listened to the officer's testimony.
sentences.zh: 我还看到来自佛罗里达州的民主党人斯蒂芬妮·墨菲在听取警官证词时也变得情绪激动。

sentences.en: You know, I have two young children.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有两个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: I have a 10-year-old son and a 7-year-old daughter.
sentences.zh: 我有一个10岁的儿子和一个7岁的女儿。

sentences.en: They're the light of my life.
sentences.zh: 他们是我生命中的光。

sentences.en: And the reason I was able to hug them again was because of the courage that you and your fellow officers showed that day.
sentences.zh: 我之所以能再次拥抱他们，是因为你和你的同事那天表现出的勇气。

sentences.en: And so just a really heartfelt thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以，衷心地感谢你们。

sentences.en: And if you didn't know any better, you would just have watched this committee and thought this was a traditional bipartisan committee
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道内情，你只会看着这个委员会，认为这是一个传统的两党委员会，

sentences.en: trying to get to the facts about what happened during a tragic attack on the nation's capital.
sentences.zh: 试图查明在这场针对国家首都的悲剧性袭击中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: But as this very somber, fact-finding description of the violence of January 6th is going on inside this hearing room, outside is a completely different reality.
sentences.zh: 但是，当这种关于1月6日暴力的沉重、事实调查描述在听证室内进行时，外面却是完全不同的现实。

sentences.en: This committee is completely partisan from top to bottom.
sentences.zh: 这个委员会从头到尾完全是党派性的。

sentences.en: There is a reason that Nancy Pelosi is the most disliked elected official in America.
sentences.zh: 南希·佩洛西成为美国最不受欢迎的民选官员是有原因的。

sentences.en: She doesn't want the American people to know the truth or learn the facts.
sentences.zh: 她不想让美国人民知道真相或了解事实。

sentences.en: Speaker Pelosi wants her narrative and her outcome to prevail and not the truth.
sentences.zh: 佩洛西议长希望她的叙事和结果占上风，而不是真相。

sentences.en: She doesn't want a fair or bipartisan investigation.
sentences.zh: 她不想要一个公平或两党参与的调查。

sentences.en: She wants a political one.
sentences.zh: 她想要一个政治性的调查。

sentences.en: That becomes a failed committee and a failed report, a sham that no one can believe.
sentences.zh: 那将成为一个失败的委员会和一份失败的报告，一个没人能相信的骗局。

sentences.en: The Republican leadership of the House of Representatives was just an hour before the hearing began, condemning the panel that was hearing it as a partisan exercise and a sham.
sentences.zh: 众议院的共和党领导层在听证会开始前一小时，就谴责听证小组是党派操弄和骗局。

sentences.en: So, Luke, how did we get to this point where a congressional committee devoted to trying to understand what happened on January 6th
sentences.zh: 那么，卢克，我们是如何走到这一步的，一个致力于试图了解1月6日发生了什么

sentences.en: and who is responsible for it devolved into this bizarre split-screen universe?
sentences.zh: 以及谁该负责的国会委员会，演变成了这种奇怪的分裂宇宙？

sentences.en: Well, shortly after the attack, there was widespread agreement that it should be investigated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，袭击发生后不久，人们普遍认为应该进行调查。

sentences.en: Kevin McCarthy, the leader of the Republicans in the House, said that President Trump bore responsibility for the violence.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党领袖凯文·麦卡锡表示，特朗普总统对暴力事件负有责任。

sentences.en: The president bears responsibility for Wednesday's attack on Congress by mob rioters.
sentences.zh: 总统对周三暴徒袭击国会负有责任。

sentences.en: And that there should be a fact-finding commission to investigate it.
sentences.zh: 并且应该成立一个事实调查委员会来调查此事。

sentences.en: January 6th was a disgrace.
sentences.zh: 1月6日是一个耻辱。

sentences.en: Leader McConnell, the leader of the Senate Republicans, said that President Trump was not off the hook.
sentences.zh: 参议院共和党领袖麦康奈尔表示，特朗普总统并没有脱离干系。

sentences.en: President Trump is still liable for everything he did while he was in office.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对他任期内所做的一切仍然负有责任。

sentences.en: Didn't get away with anything yet.
sentences.zh: 还没有逃脱任何惩罚。

sentences.en: And one by one, you heard Republicans talking along these lines.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个，你听到共和党人沿着这些思路说话。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham said he never wanted to talk with Trump again or deal with them.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆说他再也不想和特朗普谈话或与他打交道了。

sentences.en: There was sort of this widespread belief that they were going to act in a different way than they had in the past, and this was going to change things.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种普遍的信念，认为他们会以与过去不同的方式行事，这将改变局面。

sentences.en: And they were really going to investigate how Trump radicalized a portion of the base to make them want to storm the Capitol and overturn the election.
sentences.zh: 他们真的会调查特朗普是如何激化一部分选民基础，使他们想要冲击国会大厦并推翻选举结果的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think the question back then was, how would this bipartisan consensus and this outrage over January 6th, how would it be channeled into some kind of investigative process
sentences.zh: 我认为当时的问题是，这种两党共识和对1月6日的愤怒，将如何转化为某种调查程序，

sentences.en: that matched the scale of what had happened?
sentences.zh: 以匹配所发生事件的规模？

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The first thing Democrats wanted to do was impeach the president.
sentences.zh: 民主党人想做的第一件事就是弹劾总统。

sentences.en: You'll remember back in January, about a week after the attack on the Capitol, that Democrats quickly pursued a second impeachment of former President Trump
sentences.zh: 你还记得在1月，也就是国会大厦遇袭后大约一周，民主党人迅速对前总统特朗普进行了第二次弹劾，

sentences.en: to hold him accountable under the charge of inciting an insurrection.
sentences.zh: 以煽动叛乱的罪名追究他的责任。

sentences.en: But the feeling at the time among most Republicans was that impeaching the president a second time was not a step that they wanted to take.
sentences.zh: 但当时大多数共和党人的感觉是，第二次弹劾总统不是他们想采取的步骤。

sentences.en: But they did want to get to the bottom of January 6th.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实想查清1月6日的真相。

sentences.en: There was still a lot of raw feelings about it.
sentences.zh: 对此仍然有很多强烈的情绪。

sentences.en: There was a sense that the Democratic process had been completely disrupted in a way that was unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 人们认为民主进程以一种不可接受的方式被彻底破坏了。

sentences.en: And the proposal that they had was to have a 9-11 style commission.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的建议是成立一个9·11风格的委员会。

sentences.en: And what does that mean, a 9-11 style commission?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思，9·11风格的委员会？

sentences.en: Well, the 9-11 commission was the gold standard of how to carry out a bipartisan or even nonpartisan investigation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，9·11委员会是开展两党甚至无党派调查的黄金标准。

sentences.en: It was an independent commission where Democrats and Republicans got to appoint an even number of people to the panel.
sentences.zh: 这是一个独立的委员会，民主党和共和党可以任命相同数量的人员进入该小组。

sentences.en: And they were not current lawmakers who were trying to win re-election or needed to be popular with the voters.
sentences.zh: 他们不是试图赢得连任或需要受选民欢迎的现任议员。

sentences.en: They were, for the most part, some heavy hitters who had been former senators or governors or people involved in the Watergate investigation
sentences.zh: 他们大多是一些重量级人物，曾是前参议员、州长或参与过水门事件调查的人，

sentences.en: who would now come either out of retirement or step aside to devote themselves to this sort of neutral and patriotic cause.
sentences.zh: 他们现在要么退休，要么退居二线，致力于这种中立和爱国的事业。

sentences.en: I remember one of the first meetings they had, the members of the committee were sitting as Republicans on one side,
sentences.zh: 我记得他们举行的第一次会议之一，委员会成员坐着，共和党人在一边，

sentences.en: Democrats on the other, and they were told not to do that.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在另一边，他们被告知不要那样做。

sentences.en: They were supposed to sit next to each other.
sentences.zh: 他们应该坐在一起。

sentences.en: They were supposed to not treat each other by political party.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该按政党对待彼此。

sentences.en: And it was supposed to be completely bipartisan or even nonpartisan.
sentences.zh: 它应该是完全两党甚至无党派的。

sentences.en: They spent the better part of two years investigating what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们花了近两年时间调查出了什么问题。

sentences.en: They had testimony from everybody up to the president himself and the vice president.
sentences.zh: 他们听取了从总统本人到副总统等所有人的证词。

sentences.en: And at the end of their investigation, they put together a really authoritative report that actually became a best-selling book.
sentences.zh: 在调查结束时，他们整理了一份非常有权威的报告，实际上成为了一本畅销书。

sentences.en: I remember reading it not long after I graduated from college.
sentences.zh: 我记得我大学毕业后不久就读过它。

sentences.en: And for the first time, I think I really understood what had motivated Al-Qaeda and the security breakdowns that had happened
sentences.zh: 我想我第一次真正理解了是什么激励了基地组织，以及发生的安全漏洞，

sentences.en: and how that really hampered the United States and keeping the people safe.
sentences.zh: 以及这如何真正阻碍了美国保障人民安全的能力。

sentences.en: And so those were things that I think a lot of the public learned from that report.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我认为公众从那份报告中学到的东西。

sentences.en: And I would say the most important thing was to establish a shared set of facts.
sentences.zh: 我想最重要的事情是建立一套共享的事实。

sentences.en: That the entire country, whether you're a Republican or Democrat, here was a report that everyone could agree upon.
sentences.zh: 整个国家，无论你是共和党人还是民主党人，这是一份每个人都能同意的报告。

sentences.en: It was not one side or the other telling you what happened.
sentences.zh: 这不是一方或另一方告诉你发生了什么。

sentences.en: It was the definitive document about how 9-11 happened, who was to blame, and how we can fix things.
sentences.zh: 它是关于9·11如何发生、谁该负责以及我们如何解决问题的权威文件。

sentences.en: So that is the model that both sides are saying they're ready to embrace when it comes to investigating January 6th.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是双方在调查1月6日时都表示准备接受的模式。

sentences.en: So what happens to that proposal?
sentences.zh: 那么那个提议发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, in May, Republicans have a decision to make, whether they're going to go ahead and continue with what they've said they want,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在5月，共和党人必须做出决定，他们是否要继续推进他们所说的他们想要的，

sentences.en: which is a bipartisan investigation into the January 6th attack, or are they going to listen to former President Trump,
sentences.zh: 即对1月6日袭击事件进行两党调查，还是听从前总统特朗普的意见，

sentences.en: who's been telling everybody that will listen that nothing major happened that day, that the police officers were actually embraced by, you know,
sentences.zh: 他一直在告诉所有愿意听的人，那天没有发生什么大事，警察实际上是被，你知道，

sentences.en: a beautiful crowd of peaceful supporters.
sentences.zh: 一群美丽的和平支持者所拥抱。

sentences.en: And come May, both Kevin McCarthy, who is the leader of the House Republicans, and Senator Mitch McConnell, who leads the Senate Republicans,
sentences.zh: 到了5月，众议院共和党领袖凯文·麦卡锡和参议院共和党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔，

sentences.en: decide they're going to oppose the commission.
sentences.zh: 决定他们要反对这个委员会。

sentences.en: And what's your understanding of why?
sentences.zh: 你对原因的理解是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's a completely political calculation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个完全的政治算计。

sentences.en: If you talk to Republicans, they believe that 2022 is their year to win back the House.
sentences.zh: 如果你和共和党人交谈，他们认为2022年是他们赢回众议院的一年。

sentences.en: And if you talk to them privately, they'll tell you that they know January 6th is a losing issue for them, in their view.
sentences.zh: 如果你私下和他们交谈，他们会告诉你，他们知道1月6日对他们来说是一个失败的议题。

sentences.en: They know it was President Trump's supporters who attacked the Capitol, and they think every day spent talking about January 6th
sentences.zh: 他们知道是特朗普总统的支持者袭击了国会大厦，他们认为每天谈论1月6日

sentences.en: is a reminder of the extremism of some of the Republican Party, its lockstep loyalty to Donald Trump, how that led to a very dark day in American history,
sentences.zh: 这提醒了人们共和党内部分人的极端主义，以及他们对唐纳德·特朗普亦步亦趋的忠诚，而这又是如何导致了美国历史上非常黑暗的一天，

sentences.en: an embarrassment for their party and for the country, and they don't want to talk about it anymore.
sentences.zh: 这对他们的党派和国家来说都是一种尴尬，他们不想再谈论这件事了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the House, which has the votes to do this just with the Democrats, votes to pass a September 11th-style commission.
sentences.zh: 所以，众议院仅凭民主党人的票数就足以通过这项议案，投票通过了一个类似“9·11”调查委员会的提案。

sentences.en: But by the time it gets to the Senate, it needs 10 Republicans to support it because of the Senate's filibuster rule.
sentences.zh: 但当它提交到参议院时，由于参议院的阻挠议事规则，它需要10名共和党人的支持。

sentences.en: And...
After careful consideration,
sentences.zh: 经过慎重考虑，

sentences.en: I've made the decision to oppose the House Democrats' slanted and unbalanced proposal for another commission to study the events of January the 6th.
sentences.zh: 我已决定反对众议院民主党人提出的关于成立另一个委员会来调查1月6日事件的片面且不平衡的提案。

sentences.en: Senator Mitch McConnell decides to use his first filibuster of Joe Biden's presidency against the January 6th commission.
sentences.zh: 参议员米奇·麦康奈尔决定在他乔·拜登总统任期内的首次阻挠议事中，针对1月6日调查委员会行使否决权。

sentences.en: And I'll continue to urge my colleagues to oppose this extraneous layer when the time comes for the Senate to vote.
sentences.zh: 当参议院进行投票时，我将继续敦促我的同事们反对这个多余的层级。

sentences.en: And he asks, he implores, in some telling, his colleagues to join him against what might be some of their inclinations to oppose the commission.
sentences.zh: 他要求，甚至可以说是恳求他的同事们加入他的行列，去对抗那些可能与他们反对委员会的倾向相左的意见。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 54, the nays are 35.
sentences.zh: 本次投票，赞成票54票，反对票35票。

sentences.en: The motion is not agreed to.
sentences.zh: 动议未获通过。

sentences.en: And so the measure fails in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 因此，该措施在参议院失败了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And with it, any possibility of an independent commission exploring January 6th the way an independent commission explored September 11th.
sentences.zh: 随之破灭的，还有任何像调查“9·11”事件那样，以独立委员会形式调查1月6日事件的可能性。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Luke, with the best model out there, this gold standard investigation and independent commission no longer possible, what options are left?
sentences.zh: 那么，卢克，既然最好的模式、这种黄金标准的调查和独立委员会已不再可能，还有什么选择呢？

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, there were a few options.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有几个选择。

sentences.en: President Biden could have appointed a commission.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统本可以任命一个委员会。

sentences.en: There was a presidential commission that investigated the JFK assassination and also the attack on Pearl Harbor.
sentences.zh: 曾经有一个总统委员会调查过肯尼迪遇刺案，也调查过珍珠港事件。

sentences.en: But there was some hand-wringing about if President Biden appointed it, would it look like he was investigating his predecessor?
sentences.zh: 但当时有一些顾虑，如果由拜登总统任命，看起来会不会像是在调查他的前任？

sentences.en: Maybe that would look bad.
sentences.zh: 也许那样看起来不太好。

sentences.en: So the option that Speaker Nancy Pelosi settled on was to appoint a select committee, which can be given a specific task to do with a specific focus.
sentences.zh: 所以南希·佩洛西议长最终决定任命一个特别委员会，它可以被赋予特定的任务，并专注于特定的重点。

sentences.en: So she went ahead and drafted a proposal to have a select committee, which would have eight of her appointees and five nominees from the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 于是她着手起草了一份提案，成立一个特别委员会，其中将包括她任命的八名成员和共和党提名的五名成员。

sentences.en: So bipartisan in theory.
sentences.zh: 所以理论上是两党合作的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she starts off with her eight appointees.
sentences.zh: 她首先任命了她的八名成员。

sentences.en: And then Kevin McCarthy, the Republican leader, nominates his five individuals.
sentences.zh: 然后共和党领袖凯文·麦卡锡提名了他的五个人选。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: That's when a monkey wrench gets thrown into the proceedings.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，事情出了岔子。

sentences.en: Among the five Republicans that Kevin McCarthy offered up were two that Democrats, the rank-and-file Democrats, found completely unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 在凯文·麦卡锡提名的五名共和党人中，有两人被民主党人，即普通民主党议员，认为完全不可接受。

sentences.en: And they start inundating Speaker Pelosi with calls to object to their inclusion.
sentences.zh: 他们开始不断给佩洛西议长打电话，反对将这两人纳入委员会。

sentences.en: And who are those two Republicans?
sentences.zh: 那两名共和党人是谁？

sentences.en: The first is Congressman Jim Jordan.
sentences.zh: 第一位是众议员吉姆·乔丹。

sentences.en: My hunch is the reason we didn't have the backup there for those good Capitol Hill police officers is because what happened in the summer of 2020, Laura,
sentences.zh: 我的直觉是，我们之所以没有为那些优秀的国会大厦警察提供后援，是因为2020年夏天发生的事情，劳拉，

sentences.en: Democrats normalized anarchy.
sentences.zh: 民主党人让无政府状态常态化了。

sentences.en: Who Democrats objected to in part because he met with Donald Trump in December and helped plan the objections to the election on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 民主党人反对他，部分原因是他在12月会见了唐纳德·特朗普，并帮助策划了对1月6日选举结果的异议。

sentences.en: They said he was a potential witness that the committee could call and therefore could not serve on the committee.
sentences.zh: 他们说他是一个潜在的证人，委员会可能会传唤他，因此他不能在委员会任职。

sentences.en: Passing.
sentences.zh: 通过。

sentences.en: The other was Congressman Jim Banks.
sentences.zh: 另一位是众议员吉姆·班克斯。

sentences.en: The more you ask these questions and unravel the facts about January 6th, the more you get into a line of questions that go up a chain of command
sentences.zh: 你问的问题越多，揭开的关于1月6日的事实越多，你就越会陷入一系列指向指挥链的问题，

sentences.en: that end up on Speaker Pelosi's desk.
sentences.zh: 最终指向佩洛西议长的办公桌。

sentences.en: What we know is that the Capitol...
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，国会大厦……

sentences.en: Who Democrats said disqualified himself in their view by objecting to the election, the certification of Joe Biden's victory, opposing the creation of the commission,
sentences.zh: 民主党人认为他因反对选举、反对认证乔·拜登的胜利、反对成立委员会而失去了资格，

sentences.en: and then on the day he was nominated, releasing a fiery statement, in their view, undermining the committee's work and the committee's purpose.
sentences.zh: 而且在他被提名的当天，他还发表了一份激烈的声明，在他们看来，这破坏了委员会的工作和目的。

sentences.en: They have made statements and taken actions that I think would impact the integrity of the commission, of the committee.
sentences.zh: 他们发表的言论和采取的行动，我认为会影响委员会的公正性。

sentences.en: And so Speaker Pelosi says, no, neither Banks nor Jordan can serve on this committee.
sentences.zh: 所以佩洛西议长说，不行，班克斯和乔丹都不能在这个委员会任职。

sentences.en: It's my responsibility as Speaker of the House to make sure we get to the truth on this and we will not let their antics stand in the way.
sentences.zh: 作为众议院议长，我有责任确保我们查明真相，我们不会让他们的胡闹阻碍我们。

sentences.en: But even if you accept the Democrats' critiques for a moment, that these two House Republicans cannot possibly be objective about January 6th
sentences.zh: 但即使你暂时接受民主党人的批评，认为这两位共和党众议员不可能对1月6日事件保持客观，

sentences.en: because of their conduct, because of their statements, they are still members of Congress, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他们的行为，因为他们的言论，他们仍然是国会议员，对吧？

sentences.en: And they were chosen by their leader.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是由他们的领袖选出来的。

sentences.en: So can Pelosi just block them from this committee like that?
sentences.zh: 那么佩洛西就这样把他们挡在委员会之外，真的可以吗？

sentences.en: Well, she can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她可以。

sentences.en: It turns out, it was sort of in the fine print of the bill, that Speaker Pelosi had veto power over Leader McCarthy's choices.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，法案的细则里写着，佩洛西议长对麦卡锡领袖的选择拥有否决权。

sentences.en: And so while he could nominate, she had to concur.
sentences.zh: 所以虽然他可以提名，但她必须同意。

sentences.en: And he says that this shows, in his view, that Speaker Pelosi was only interested in a partisan game and not interested in really getting to the facts.
sentences.zh: 他说，这在他看来表明，佩洛西议长只对党派游戏感兴趣，而不是真的想查明事实。

sentences.en: And so when she nixed two of his nominees, he decided to pull all five of his from the committee, leaving the committee with not a single nominee from the Republican leader.
sentences.zh: 所以当她否决了他的两名提名人选时，他决定撤回他所有的五名提名人，导致委员会里连一名共和党领袖提名的人都没有。

sentences.en: And so, Luke, who's ultimately left on this committee that Speaker Pelosi had said at the outset was meant to be bipartisan?
sentences.zh: 那么，卢克，最终留在委员会里的还有谁呢？佩洛西议长起初可是说这个委员会旨在实现两党合作的。

sentences.en: So Speaker Pelosi did something interesting when she appointed her eight members.
sentences.zh: 所以佩洛西议长在任命她的八名成员时做了一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: She appointed seven Democrats, but she also appointed one Republican herself.
sentences.zh: 她任命了七名民主党人，但她自己也任命了一名共和党人。

sentences.en: She nominated Liz Cheney, the former third-ranking Republican of the House,
sentences.zh: 她提名了利兹·切尼，这位众议院排名第三的前共和党领导人，

sentences.en: whose constant criticism and scrutiny of Donald Trump and his actions caused her to be ousted from House Republican leadership.
sentences.zh: 她对唐纳德·特朗普及其行为的持续批评和审视，导致她被逐出了众议院共和党领导层。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now Nancy Pelosi has a choice to make.
sentences.zh: 现在南希·佩洛西面临一个选择。

sentences.en: Now she has five empty slots on the committee.
sentences.zh: 现在委员会里有五个空缺名额。

sentences.en: And so she looks around and thinks, who else can I appoint to make this more bipartisan?
sentences.zh: 于是她环顾四周，心想，我还能任命谁来让它看起来更具两党色彩？

sentences.en: And there's only one other Republican who voted to create the select committee, and that is Adam Kinzinger of Illinois, a six-term congressman, a former Air Force veteran,
sentences.zh: 还有另一位投票支持成立特别委员会的共和党人，那就是伊利诺伊州的亚当·金辛格，一位连任六届的国会议员，前空军退伍军人，

sentences.en: who has emerged as another forceful critic of Donald Trump and a person who has urged his party to move in a different direction
sentences.zh: 他已成为唐纳德·特朗普的另一位强力批评者，并敦促他的党派朝着不同的方向前进，

sentences.en: than marching in lockstep with the former president.
sentences.zh: 而不是与前总统亦步亦趋。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: So basically Pelosi looks around the entire House Republican caucus and can only find two members that are acceptable to her members and who are actually willing, it seems,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，佩洛西环顾整个众议院共和党核心小组，只能找到两名她的成员可以接受，而且看起来确实愿意，

sentences.en: to serve on this select committee investigating January 6th.
sentences.zh: 在调查1月6日的特别委员会中任职的成员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what we're left with is a select committee investigating the causes and failures of the January 6th riot of the Capitol
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终得到的是一个调查1月6日国会大厦骚乱起因和失职的特别委员会，

sentences.en: that the vast majority of congressional Republicans don't support and are now denouncing, right?
sentences.zh: 绝大多数国会共和党人并不支持它，现在还在谴责它，对吧？

sentences.en: And that is constituted almost entirely by Democrats and, by the way, is four members short of its original plan.
sentences.zh: 而且它几乎完全由民主党人组成，顺便说一句，比原计划少了四名成员。

sentences.en: And so it feels like all of this drama you're describing reveals just how much this January 6th investigative process
sentences.zh: 所以感觉你描述的所有这些戏剧性事件都揭示了，这个1月6日的调查过程，

sentences.en: probably really needed to be in the hands of an independent 9-11-style commission rather than in the hands of sitting lawmakers with their very partisan instincts.
sentences.zh: 可能真的需要掌握在独立的“9·11”式委员会手中，而不是掌握在那些带有强烈党派本能的在职议员手中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: This has devolved into the exact scenario that many people from, frankly, both sides of the aisle are worried about.
sentences.zh: 这已经演变成了许多人，坦率地说，两党人士都担心的那种局面。

sentences.en: So given this very weird, less-than-ideal committee makeup, what is this committee actually going to try to do to reveal the information they're after
sentences.zh: 那么，考虑到这个非常奇怪、不太理想的委员会构成，这个委员会实际上打算做些什么来揭示他们所追求的信息，

sentences.en: and what kind of power do we expect them to actually have?
sentences.zh: 我们预计他们实际上拥有什么样的权力？

sentences.en: Well, they have subpoena power and they're going to follow two key lines of inquiry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们拥有传唤权，他们将遵循两条关键的调查路线。

sentences.en: The first are security breakdowns that occurred that day.
sentences.zh: 第一条是那天发生的安保漏洞。

sentences.en: The other is why did the attackers do what they did?
sentences.zh: 另一条是袭击者为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: Who helped organize the rally?
sentences.zh: 谁帮助组织了集会？

sentences.en: Who motivated them?
sentences.zh: 谁激励了他们？

sentences.en: Who incited them?
sentences.zh: 谁煽动了他们？

sentences.en: So all of those questions go into a second line of inquiry that is likely to result in subpoenas for documents and for testimony.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些问题都归入第二条调查路线，很可能会导致对文件和证词的传唤。

sentences.en: And when we say subpoenas, do we know yet who this committee may try to subpoena?
sentences.zh: 当我们说传唤时，我们知道委员会可能会试图传唤谁吗？

sentences.en: We don't yet, but we do know some likely suspects.
sentences.zh: 我们还不知道，但我们确实知道一些可能的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: President Trump, his inner circle, and anyone who talked to him that day and the buildup to that day.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统、他的核心圈子，以及那天和在那天之前与他交谈过的任何人。

sentences.en: We know that Leader McCarthy had an angry phone call with President Trump that day.
sentences.zh: 我们知道麦卡锡领袖那天和特朗普总统通过一次愤怒的电话。

sentences.en: I'm sure the committee will be interested in that.
sentences.zh: 我相信委员会会对那次通话感兴趣。

sentences.en: We know that several senators were on the phone with President Trump that day.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那天有几位参议员和特朗普总统通过电话。

sentences.en: They may be called to testify.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会被传唤作证。

sentences.en: There have been accusations that certain sitting members of Congress helped plan the rally that preceded the attack on the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 有指控称，某些在职国会议员帮助策划了袭击国会大厦前的集会。

sentences.en: They may well be on a witness liSt.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能在证人名单上。

sentences.en: So we don't know exactly who will be called yet, but we do know the committee is fully empowered to seek answers, and they have the power of law behind them now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还不知道具体会传唤谁，但我们确实知道委员会已被充分授权去寻求答案，而且他们现在拥有法律的力量作为后盾。

sentences.en: And so is it possible that this committee will hear from former President Trump?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个委员会是否有可能听取前总统特朗普的证词？

sentences.en: It's a distinct possibility that they will subpoena former President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们传唤前总统特朗普的可能性很大。

sentences.en: Whether or not he complies is another question, but the reason they want to hear from former President Trump is they want to know about his mindset, who he talked with,
sentences.zh: 他是否会遵守是另一回事，但他们想听取前总统特朗普证词的原因是，他们想了解他的心态，他与谁交谈过，

sentences.en: what decisions he made, and why he didn't call off the attack much earlier.
sentences.zh: 他做了什么决定，以及为什么他没有更早地叫停袭击。

sentences.en: So they have serious questions for him, and they want to hear serious answers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有严肃的问题要问他，他们想听到严肃的回答。

sentences.en: Luke, based on what you saw on day one of this committee's work, do you think it has any real chance of succeeding in its mission
sentences.zh: 卢克，根据你在该委员会工作第一天所看到的，你认为它有任何真正的机会成功完成其使命吗？

sentences.en: of trying to get to the bottom of what happened on January 6th?
sentences.zh: 即试图查明1月6日到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Based on what I saw today, this committee is approaching its work in a serious fashion.
sentences.zh: 根据我今天所看到的，这个委员会正在以严肃的态度开展工作。

sentences.en: They had revelatory testimony today that did get to the heart of the trauma and violence of January 6th, and they did it in a sober way
sentences.zh: 他们今天听取了揭示性的证词，确实触及了1月6日创伤和暴力的核心，而且他们是以一种冷静的方式做到的，

sentences.en: where they were not distracted by partisan antics and partisan politics.
sentences.zh: 没有被党派的胡闹和党派政治所干扰。

sentences.en: That said, when you look back at how the 9-11 Commission did its work with an independent body, that commission had the mandate to be trusted
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，当你回顾“9·11”委员会是如何以一个独立机构开展工作时，那个委员会拥有被两党、被各界美国人信任的使命，

sentences.en: by both parties, by Americans of all stripes.
sentences.zh: 而这个委员会，即使它以最严肃、冷静、公正、实事求是的方式开展工作，也始终面临着被半个国家视为党派工具的风险。

sentences.en: And this committee, even if it does its work in the most serious, sober, fair-minded, fact-finding way, runs the risk of always being seen
sentences.zh: 而我不确定你该如何改变这一点。

sentences.en: by half the country as a partisan exercise.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure how you change that.
sentences.zh: 尽管共和党领导人，卢克，正在拒绝这个委员会，

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 也许这个委员会最终正是那些共和党领导人想要的。

sentences.en: Even though Republican leaders, Luke, are rejecting this committee,
sentences.zh: 一个可能会产生新事实、可能会发掘出非常重要信息的委员会，但随后可以被斥为党派偏见。

sentences.en: maybe this committee ultimately is exactly what those Republican leaders wanted.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想如果你纯粹从党派的角度来看待这个问题，并且考虑到2022年的选举，你最大的担忧是可能会揭露出新的事实，

sentences.en: A committee that might produce new facts, might unearth really important information, but can then be dismissed as partisan.
sentences.zh: 让你的党派看起来很糟糕，那么这也会是一种成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess if you're looking at this through a purely partisan lens, and with 2022 on your mind, and your greatest concern is that new facts may be uncovered
sentences.zh: 我只是不确定这是否是大多数非政治化的美国人所认同的成功定义。

sentences.en: that make your party look bad, then that would be a form of success.
sentences.zh: 我不确定对于那天在国会大厦的人们，那些为逃命而奔逃的议员，以及那些在暴徒手中遭受了巨大痛苦的警察来说，这是成功的定义。

sentences.en: I'm just not sure it's the definition of success that most non-political Americans would agree to.
sentences.zh: 好吧，卢克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I'm not sure it's the definition of success for the people who were in the Capitol that day, the lawmakers who fled for their lives, and the officers who suffered so greatly
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: at the hands of the mob.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Well, Luke, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 周二，联邦卫生官员发布了关于口罩的新指南，反映了他们对新冠病毒德尔塔变异株日益增长的担忧。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 官员们表示，在感染激增的地区，即使是接种过新冠疫苗的人，也应该在室内公共场所恢复佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 随着新学年的临近，官员们敦促所有教师、员工和学生，无论疫苗接种情况或地点如何，都要佩戴口罩。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, federal health officials issued new guidelines on masks that reflect their growing fears over the Delta variant of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 我只想说明，这不是我们或疾控中心轻易做出的决定。

sentences.en: The officials said that in areas of the country where infections are surging, even people vaccinated against COVID-19 should resume wearing masks in indoor public spaces.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这让我感到压力很大。

sentences.en: And with the school year approaching, the officials urged all teachers, staff, and students to wear masks regardless of vaccine status or location.
sentences.zh: 在新闻发布会上，疾控中心主任罗谢尔·瓦伦斯基表示，该指南的动机是新的证据表明，在极少数情况下，

sentences.en: I just want to indicate that this is not a decision that we or CDC have made lightly.
sentences.zh: 即使是接种过疫苗的人也可能感染德尔塔变异株，可能携带大量病毒，并能传播病毒。

sentences.en: This weighs heavily on me, I know.
sentences.zh: 这项新的科学发现令人担忧，不幸的是，它需要我们更新建议。

sentences.en: During a news conference, the head of the CDC, Rochelle Walensky, said that the guidance was motivated by new evidence that in rare cases,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在相关政策调整方面，

sentences.en: even vaccinated people can become infected by the Delta variant, may carry large amounts of the virus, and can spread it.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统正在考虑要求所有联邦工作人员接种疫苗或定期接受新冠检测，这在之前是拜登曾表示反对的事情。

sentences.en: This new science is worrisome and unfortunately warrants an update to our recommendation.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由奥斯汀·米切尔制作，

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in a related policy shift,
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: President Biden is considering requiring that all federal workers be vaccinated or submit to regular COVID-19 testing, something that Biden had previously said that he opposed.
sentences.zh: 我们明天再见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。
